edbDesc: An optical and electrical phenomenon whereby a beam of electrons is generated by an electron gun (e.g. cathode ray tube) and then impacts on a luminescent material such as a phosphor, causing the material to emit visible light. The most common example is the screen of a television.
title: Cathodoluminescence
pickWhy: Plücker's Electricity in a vacuum card is the green glow when cathode rays strike glass.
